issue.title: Bug: Tool responses with mixed content incorrectly identified as user messages in OpenAI format

steps: Create a directory `docs` containing three markdown files `guide.md`, `api.md` and `faq.md`, each with at least 60 lines of descriptive text about a fictional command-line tool called widgetctl.
use read_many_files to look at the docs dir summarize
expected: The read_many_files result is sent back to the model as a tool message answering the tool_call_id, and the agent summarizes the docs.
defect: The mixed tool result (one functionResponse part plus text parts) is converted to a `role: 'user'` message instead of a tool message, so OpenAI-format endpoints reject the request ("An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'", surfaced as `400 status code (no body)`).

fault location.explanation: For mixed part lists only function calls are tracked (hasAIContent), so functionResponse + text parts fall through to speaker 'human'; PR #415 adds hasToolContent and returns speaker 'tool' when any functionResponse is present.
Marks user-role content as tool only when every block is a tool_response (blocks.every), so tool_response + text blocks stay human; PR #415 switches to blocks.some().

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/415. When read_many_files returns large output, the tool result is a part list with one functionResponse plus several text parts. In v0.4.7, GeminiChat.convertPartListUnionToIContent handles this 'mixed' case by setting the speaker to 'ai' only if a functionCall is present and otherwise defaulting to 'human', and ContentConverters.toIContent only upgrades a user-role content to the 'tool' speaker when all blocks are tool_response. Both paths therefore classify the tool result as a human message, the OpenAI provider serializes it as `role: 'user'`, and the assistant tool_call is left without a matching tool message, which strict OpenAI-compatible APIs reject with HTTP 400. Commit e170bc6 (PR #415) tracks hasToolContent and prefers the 'tool' speaker in geminiChat.ts, and uses blocks.some() in ContentConverters.ts (it also adds a --dumponerror debug flag, unrelated to the defect). The fix first ships in v0.4.8; the pinned v0.11.0 contains it, so the case is tested at v0.4.7, the latest release before the issue was opened on 2025-11-01.
